C-ZXC-001.description_zh: 六经皆史也：古人未尝离事而言理，六经皆先王之政典。经的神圣性不在于超验教条，而在于它们是曾经运作过的制度与事务的记录——道在事中，即器存道。此法把一切「经典」还原为「史料」，把义理之辩还原为对具体政事实践的理解，釜底抽薪地取消了空谈心性与悬空立说的合法性。

C-ZXC-002.description_zh: 圆神而撰，方智以记：史有二体——《尚书》圆而神，《春秋》方以智。「撰述」是成一家之言的创造性著作，需别识心裁、因事命篇、不为成法所拘；「记注」是史官有定律的资料保存。混淆二者则产生以考据琐碎冒充著述、或以空论冒充著作的双重弊病。此法为知识生产确立了「资料层」与「创作层」的分工界面。

C-ZXC-003.description_zh: 才学识三长，得一犹不易，而史德尤为其要：能具史识者，必知史德；德者何？谓著书者之心术也。史家之病不在公然伪造事实，而在「似公实私」——以理抗势易，以理制情难；文章之士务求胜人而不惧其偏。故须「慎辨于天人之际，尽其天而不益以人」：把史家主观的「人」压到最低，让事实之「天」自己显现。

C-ZXC-004.description_zh: 独断之学与考索之功，非但用功有难易，抑且用心有深浅：高明者多独断之学，沉潜者尚考索之功。学问之可贵的不是材料的堆集，而是「别识心裁」——从材料中见出他人未见之条理与问题，作成一家之言。考据家以驳杂为博、以絮募为功，实为学之蔽。此法把「提问的原创性」置于「答案的完整性」之上。

C-ZXC-005.description_zh: 道不离器，犹影不离形：道因器而显，不因器而亡。天下岂有离器言道、离形存影者哉？道不能离开具体的制度、事业、器物而独存；同样，「理」不能离开事象独谈。宋明理学悬「道」于空言，恰是离器言道之病。此法把一切抽象原理落实为「在何种具体结构中运作」的追问，是清代「实学」转向的哲学基础。

C-ZXC-006.title_zh: C-ZXC-006: 辨章学术考镜源流法
C-ZXC-006.description_zh: 校雠之义，盖自刘向父子：部次条别，将以辨章学术，考镜源流。目录不是图书清单，而是知识谱系的地图：通过分类结构与源流梳理，呈现一门学问如何发生、分派、传承、亡佚。非深明于道术精微、群言得失之故者，不足与言校雠。此法把知识组织本身升级为一门研究方法——以结构理解内容。

C-ZXC-007.description_zh: 方志乃一方全史：志（著述正文，仿纪传之体）、掌故（典章制度档案，仿会要之体）、文征（诗文汇录，仿文选之体）三书并立。旧志以地理书、图经自限，实为大谬。此法把地方从「行政区划」升格为「完整的史料单元」，为地方建立与国家正史同构的知识工程：一地之叙事、制度、文献各有其载体，相互独立又互相印证。

C-ZXC-008.description_zh: 通史之修，其为用有二：一者仍守先正成法，述而不作；二者通古今之变，成一家之言。断代为史各不相谋，通史家必须「会通」：于全史大势中安放每一时段，使各段互为照应。史以事义为经，不以朝代为界。此法反对把知识切成互不相干的断代孤岛，主张纵向贯通之「通」。

C-ZXC-009.description_zh: 文德即敬恕：敬则不苟，恕则公——「论古必恕」，非宽容之谓，谓能为古人设身而处地。批评任何作者，必须先还原其所处之情境与所对之问题，不以后见之明苛责前人。凡为文者必敬其事、恕其人：敬是不苟且下笔，恕是不轻易断人。此法把「理解先于评判」确立为批评的铁律。

C-ZXC-010.title_zh: C-ZXC-010: 学术为公·嘉惠后学法
C-ZXC-010.description_zh: 学业将以救风气之敝，而风气之所由敝，正坐学术不明之故。学问非一人之私产：藏之名山、传之其人，「经世」之志不在当世得名，而在嘉惠后学。章学诚一生依人篱下、著述难刊，仍以「身后之名」自期，把完成体系置于当世荣辱之上。此法把学术的回报周期拉长到身后，以对抗流俗评价的短期主义。

C-ZXC-001.title_en: C-ZXC-001: All Six Classics Are History Method
C-ZXC-001.description_en: 'All the Six Classics are history': the ancients never discoursed on principle apart from affairs; the Classics are records of the governance of former kings. The authority of a classic lies not in transcendent dogma but in its being a record of institutions once in operation—Dao resides in affairs. This method reduces 'classics' to 'historical sources,' grounding principle in concrete institutional practice and deflating empty theorizing.

C-ZXC-002.title_en: C-ZXC-002: Creative Composition vs. Documentary Registration Method
C-ZXC-002.description_en: History has two genres: 'creative composition' (yuan er shen, after the Documents) — one's own voice, shaped by insight, free of fixed formula — and 'documentary registration' (fang yi zhi, after the Spring and Autumn) — rule-bound preservation by the historiographical office. Confusing them produces both pedantry masquerading as authorship and empty discourse masquerading as books. This method defines the interface between the data layer and the creation layer of knowledge production.

C-ZXC-003.title_en: C-ZXC-003: Historical Virtue Method (Cultivating the Historian's Heart)
C-ZXC-003.description_en: To the three classical qualifications (talent, learning, insight) Zhang adds 'historical virtue' — the rectitude of the author's heart. The danger is not crude falsification but 'seemingly impartial yet privately motivated' writing: resisting power with principle is easy; restraining one's own partiality is hard. Hence 'carefully discern the boundary between the natural (tian) and the human (ren): exhaust what is natural and add nothing human' — minimize the historian's subjectivity so facts may show themselves.

C-ZXC-004.description_en: 'Original judgment' (duanxue) and 'investigative labor' (kaosuo) differ not only in difficulty but in the depth of mind required. The bold excel at original judgment; the thorough at investigation. The value of scholarship lies not in heaped material but in bieshi xincai — seeing structure and questions others miss, and making one's own voice. This method ranks originality of questioning above completeness of answer.

C-ZXC-005.title_en: C-ZXC-005: Dao Inseparable from Vessels Method
C-ZXC-005.description_en: Dao is inseparable from vessels as shadow from form: Dao manifests through vessels and perishes not with any one vessel. There is no speaking of Dao apart from concrete institutions, undertakings, and things. Neo-Confucianism's suspension of Dao in empty discourse is precisely the disease of separating Dao from vessels. This method converts every abstract principle into the question: in what concrete structure does it operate?

C-ZXC-006.title_en: C-ZXC-006: Genealogy of Knowledge Method (Bianzhang Kaojing)
C-ZXC-006.description_en: The purpose of bibliographic collation, since Liu Xiang and Liu Xin, is 'to delineate the scholarship and mirror its sources' — a catalogue is not an inventory but a genealogical map of knowledge, showing how a discipline arose, branched, was transmitted, and was lost. This method upgrades knowledge organization itself into a research method: understanding content through structure.

C-ZXC-007.description_en: A gazetteer is the complete history of a locality: three parallel books — the main chronicle (after the dynastic histories), institutional records (zhanggu, after the compendia), and literary collection (wenzheng, after the anthologies). Old gazetteers wrongly limited themselves to geography. This method upgrades the locality into a complete evidential unit, an isomorphic knowledge project mirroring the national history.

C-ZXC-008.description_en: Compiling general history serves two aims: preserving ancestral method by transmitting without inventing, or comprehending change across past and present to make one's own voice. Dynastic histories never talk to each other; the general historian must 'conjoin' (huitong), placing every period within the whole's trajectory. History is threaded by affairs and meanings, not by dynastic boundaries.

C-ZXC-009.title_en: C-ZXC-009: Literary Virtue of Reverence and Forbearance Method
C-ZXC-009.description_en: Literary virtue is reverence (jing) and empathetic forbearance (shu): reverence forbids careless writing; forbearance means 'in judging antiquity, one must be shu' — not leniency but the capacity to place oneself in the ancients' situation. Before criticizing any author, reconstruct their context and the problem they faced; never judge predecessors with hindsight. Understanding precedes judgment.

C-ZXC-010.title_en: C-ZXC-010: Scholarship as Public Legacy Method
C-ZXC-010.description_en: Learning exists to remedy the diseases of the age, which stem from obscured scholarship. Knowledge is no private possession: to bequeath it to later learners is the true statecraft of the scholar. Zhang, dependent on patrons all his life and rarely published in his day, staked himself on posthumous recognition, valuing completing his system above contemporary applause — stretching the reward horizon of scholarship beyond one's own lifetime.
